# Captain Saul

## Overview

- **Age:** Seventy-six  <sub>[v4 c8 P63](../source/v04-c08.md#nw-v04-c08-p0063)</sub>
- **Gender:** Male  <sub>[v4 c6 P14](../source/v04-c06.md#nw-v04-c06-p0014)</sub>
- **Status:** Deceased  <sub>[v4 c39 P28](../source/v04-c39.md#nw-v04-c39-p0028)</sub>
- **Role:** Lighthouse keeper, former sea captain  <sub>[v4 c6 P18](../source/v04-c06.md#nw-v04-c06-p0018), [v4 c6 P20](../source/v04-c06.md#nw-v04-c06-p0020), [v4 c8 P63](../source/v04-c08.md#nw-v04-c08-p0063), [v4 c11 P33](../source/v04-c11.md#nw-v04-c11-p0033)</sub>
- **Titles:** Captain Saul  <sub>[v4 c6 P10](../source/v04-c06.md#nw-v04-c06-p0010)</sub>; Captain Garrick  <sub>[v4 c24 P33](../source/v04-c24.md#nw-v04-c24-p0033)</sub>

## Appearance

Captain Saul is a tall, plain-looking, slightly stooped man of immense strength and endurance. He has an iron-gray mane of thick hair hanging down to his shoulders, thin jaws, a rough mouth, and a broad forehead on a bronzed, heavily furrowed face. His deep-set, blue eyes twinkle, dream, and search the sea.

_Sources: [v4 c6 P14](../source/v04-c06.md#nw-v04-c06-p0014), [v4 c6 P15](../source/v04-c06.md#nw-v04-c06-p0015)_

## Personality

Possessing everlasting youth in his heart, Captain Saul is a high-souled, simple-minded, and cheerful man who holds a deep adoration for beauty. He maintains an unflappable, gentle demeanor and constant good humor that resists all attempts to anger him. Although tender and respectful toward women, he exhibits fierce indignation toward anyone who speaks ill of them. He is deeply compassionate to people and animals alike, unselfishly giving up his own comfort for others.

_Sources: [v4 c6 P13](../source/v04-c06.md#nw-v04-c06-p0013), [v4 c6 P14](../source/v04-c06.md#nw-v04-c06-p0014), [v4 c6 P23](../source/v04-c06.md#nw-v04-c06-p0023), [v4 c6 P24](../source/v04-c06.md#nw-v04-c06-p0024), [v4 c8 P61](../source/v04-c08.md#nw-v04-c08-p0061), [v4 c9 P5](../source/v04-c09.md#nw-v04-c09-p0005), [v4 c9 P48](../source/v04-c09.md#nw-v04-c09-p0048), [v4 c9 P59](../source/v04-c09.md#nw-v04-c09-p0059), [v4 c17 P16](../source/v04-c17.md#nw-v04-c17-p0016), [v4 c17 P17](../source/v04-c17.md#nw-v04-c17-p0017), [v4 c17 P18](../source/v04-c17.md#nw-v04-c17-p0018)_

- To ensure his lost love Margaret is remembered after his death  <sub>[v4 c20 P15](../source/v04-c20.md#nw-v04-c20-p0015)</sub>
- To have his life's exploits written down properly in a book  <sub>[v4 c25 P1](../source/v04-c25.md#nw-v04-c25-p0001)</sub>

## History

After spending over fifty years traveling the world as a sea captain, Captain Saul retired to Seven Gulls to tend the light at the Point. When Hugh and Nell Carrow moved to the small house by the harbor, he welcomed them warmheartedly, sharing trout, telling them ancient local lore, and becoming a beloved visitor. He entertained them with his fiddle, shared wild tales of his life at sea, and allowed Nell to read his cherished logbook. During a visit from Adrian Treleaven, Captain Saul recognized him as the schoolmaster's grandson and gladly entrusted his logbook to Adrian and Nell to be adapted into a novel. He spent a joyful summer acting as an advisor while Adrian wrote in the lighthouse's small side room. In his final years, he maintained his quiet habits at the lighthouse and took great pride when political news favored his party. Shortly after receiving the published copy of his biography, Captain Saul passed away peacefully on his couch holding the book, and was buried in the cemetery above the harbor.
